bib.title: Critical-State RL: Diagnosing Trainable States for Multi-Turn Tool Use

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Critical-State RL: Diagnosing Trainable States for Multi-Turn Tool Use", Zixiang Chen (first author), Wenting Zhao, Zhepeng Cen, et al., Salesforce AI Research (last author Huan Wang). arXiv:2609.24985v1 [cs.LG], 21 Sep 2026 (September 2026). Preprint, no venue stated.
COVERAGE: 31 of 31 pages, 97,565 of 97,565 chars. Pages 9-10 are references, which I skimmed. Pages 29-31 are prompts and code strings, which I skimmed. Everything else I read in full, including appendices A-E. Notes 04, 05, 07, 08 and 10 were not opened.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Selected-turn training beats the alternative turn in all four BFCL cells. The effect is large for miss_func and "directional" for miss_param.
 number: miss_func recovery 0.14→0.283±0.015 (+14.3pp); miss_func decision 0.14→0.095 (-4.5pp); miss_param decision 0.435→0.473±0.010 (+3.8pp); miss_param recovery 0.435→0.445 (+1pp)
 setup: no-think Gemma-4-26B-A4B, BFCL v4 multi_turn, 200 paired items, deterministic decoding, checkpoint at step 30. Selected cells use 4 training seeds {42,123,7,99}. Alternatives are single-seed point estimates.
 quote: "Recovery improves miss_func by 14.3 ±1.5 pp but leaves miss_param flat at +1 pp; decision improves miss_param by 3.8±1.0 pp but moves miss_func down by 4.5 pp." (p6)
 bears on: 04 (credit assignment), 05
2. Critical-state selection rule: rank candidate occurrences by corrected action-dependent variance, Var_a E[z|x,a]. Training-free; nested sampling of actions, then continuations per action.
 number: Table 1 mean corrected action variance: 0.0267 vs 0.0103 (miss_func), 0.0361 vs 0.0000 (miss_param). Gate: selected occurrence has the higher estimate in both categories.
 setup: 8 actions × 4 continuations per scenario, 64 scenarios per cell (54 for miss_param recovery), base policy.
 quote: "the diagnostic ranks qualifying occurrences under a common label by arg max turn t Var a t E[z|x t, a t]" (p4)
 Three gates (Def. 1, App. B.1): action-sufficiency (the label mediates action→return), headroom (some action beats the reference policy by Δ_head>0), trainability (Var_a Q>0). Estimator: V̂_act = S²_between − S²_within/m. It is unbiased but can go negative.
 bears on: 04, 07
3. Critical-State RL beats full multi-turn Monte-Carlo return-to-go credit, and beats targeted SFT on miss_func.
 number: RTG gym val 0.997 vs 0.77 for the bandit, but BFCL miss_param 0.45 (+1.5pp) vs 0.473 (+3.8pp). Targeted SFT (single seed): best recovery checkpoint 6pp below base on miss_func; +3pp on miss_param.
 setup: single-seed comparators, Gemma, miss_param non-saturated cell.
 quote: "RTG reaches a gym validation score of 0.997 (versus 0.77 for the bandit), but its BFCL accuracy is 0.45" (p7)
 Turn-mask control: full, recovery, random and decision masks with trajectory-level A=R−b all leave miss_param near start. This suggests the gain comes from the local label, not from the mask.
 bears on: 04, 07
4. Compute cost. One whole-trajectory optimizer step cost 16–30× an occurrence-local RL step in the Nemotron comparison.
 number: 16–30×
 setup: Nemotron-Super-120B. LoRA rank 64, α=256, GRPO+DAPO dynamic sampling, NeMo-RL. LR 5e-6, KL coefficient 0, 64 prompts × 32 generations per step. No GPU counts or hours are given.
 quote: "a whole-trajectory optimizer step cost 16–30× as much as an occurrence-local RL step" (p18)
 bears on: 10
5. Other applications (not matched tests of the diagnostic).
 - Nemotron miss_func: 0.408±0.013→0.452±0.021 (+4.4pt, n=3 eval repeats, trains the decision turn); hospital-ward transfer 0.425→0.475 (+5.0pt, single eval).
 - Memory, BFCL v4 agentic/memory sub-task mean: xLAM (internal Qwen3-235B-A22B fine-tune) 34.54%→50.54%; Gemma 38.1%→52.7%. Trained values are single evals of selected checkpoints.
 - Repeat-call: Nemotron call/answer agreement with GPT-4.1 37%→~75% (72–78%, 3 seeds).
 - Category-routed Gemma: miss_func 0.110→0.439±0.012 (5 eval seeds). A separate run, not the four-cell study.
 quote: "The BFCL v4 agentic/memory sub-task mean moves from 34.54% for the xLAM start to 50.54% for the selected memory-trained checkpoint" (p8)
 bears on: 05, 08
6. The best training turn depends on model and task configuration. Gemma selects recovery for miss_func; Nemotron trains the decision turn. Re-diagnose per setting.
 quote: "Applying the method to a new setting therefore means reassessing the candidate calls, not reusing a fixed training turn." (p8)
 bears on: 04, 05
7. Mixed-reward groups do not imply a trainable signal. DAPO-style filtering keeps groups with Var(z|x)>0 that carry no action signal.
 number: in the Gemma pilot, every rollout is a clean refusal yet reward swings 0↔1, within-group std 0.477.
 quote: "A mixed-outcome filter would retain this group, although its reward differences do not distinguish the observed decision behavior." (p4)
 bears on: 04, 07, 08 (DAPO)
8. Theory (assumption-heavy).
 - Thm 1: best local-label gain at small KL budget ε is √(2ε·V_act).
 - Prop 2: more continuations cannot replace more actions.
 - Cor. 1 and App. E.1: broadcasting one terminal advantage across K independent occurrences adds covariance v_{−i}F_i. SNR scales 1/√K and sample cost Θ(K). An optimal constant baseline does not remove it.
 - Prop 4/5: drift outside the selected call is bounded by R_max√(2D_out).
 number: toy simulation: episodes to 0.9 accuracy for shared-return GRPO 240→1312 over K=1→32, local-label flat at ~240. Gemma home-buying S_z=0.31 (CI [0.29,0.33]), n=6560.
 Note: the K>1 results are toy or conditional. The applications use K=1.
 bears on: 04, 07

Other facts worth keeping:
- Transfer to an unseen bridge wording: 0.095→0.225 (+13.0pp), seed 123, 200 paired examples.
- Aggregate saturation: official BFCL Overall plateaus at ~59–60% over steps 25–45. Base and long_context categories fall (0.72→0.68 and 0.61→0.53) while training continues. Nemotron transfer peaks at step 15 (0.545), before the in-domain validation maximum at step 35.

How critical states are chosen: humans or deterministic rules propose the candidate phases (e.g. empty-ground-truth decision turn k−1). Failure patterns are cross-tabulated against a stronger model by BFCL error_type. Gates screen candidates, then the highest mean corrected action variance wins. Training is occurrence-local contextual-bandit RL, with gradient only on the selected call's tokens.

LIMITS (authors): the study tests categorical turn selection, not calibrated variance magnitudes or thresholds. Repeat-call, Nemotron and memory are applications, not matched tests. K=1 in the four-cell, Nemotron and memory settings. The miss_param result is "directional". Alternatives, RTG and SFT are single-seed. Evaluation noise is large: Nemotron temperature-0 runs vary by 3–5pt from serving nondeterminism. Candidate phases are human-proposed. The counterfactual check was one-way and directional, because FP8 plus expert-parallel nondeterminism made a full rerun too noisy. The xLAM checkpoint is internal and unreleased. Only one base model (Gemma-4-26B-A4B) is used for the main test. The no_write gate near 0.97 leaves little headroom there.

BUILDS ON: PivotRL (Yi et al. 2026), CSO (Critical Step Optimization), Karino et al. [47] (variance of conditional means), GRPO (Shao et al. 2024), DAPO (Yu et al. 2025), GiGPO, MT-GRPO (Wei et al. 2025), ArCHer, SWEET-RL, nested-simulation variance correction [48, 41], BFCL (Patil et al. 2025).

CODE: none worth keeping. App. F holds prompts and a reward formula: z_tool = no_write(a_dec) × consequence(y_rec) (Eq. 1, p5).

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p2) shows gradient placement across turns t0–t6, decision vs recovery. Fig 3 (p13) shows same marginal labels with different V_act (1/4 vs 1/8). Fig 4 (p19) is a concrete miss_func example. Fig 7 (p25) shows shared vs local credit variance as K grows.

PROBLEMS: none in extraction. No embedded instructions. arXiv ID and dates look unusual (2609, Sep 2026), but they are as printed. The paper has no explicit venue line and no GPU-hours figure. The extracted text is at /tmp/chen.txt.
